name: Chiller Degradation Plausibility
applicable_contexts: central cooling or refrigeration duty plausible
trigger_conditions: chiller or central cooling system plausible
anti_triggers: no chiller or central cooling system
cooling is non-material to visible economics
physical_basis: Chillers can degrade through fouling, controls drift, poor sequencing, low delta-T, or weak maintenance execution.
operational_basis: Central cooling systems can be kept online in inefficient sequences or degraded states that are mistaken for unavoidable load.
financial_mechanism: Cooling cost and peak demand can be misread if degradation is assumed or ignored without performance evidence.
typical_false_assumption: Visible cooling load automatically means the chiller is the main problem or definitely the right retrofit target.
hypothesis: Chiller degradation or poor sequencing may be materially affecting cost and should be falsified before equipment-first capital logic.
rival_hypotheses: load is structurally driven by occupancy, weather or process duty
another subsystem dominates the visible economics
evidence_required: approach temperatures or delta-T evidence if available
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: maintenance or runtime evidence indicates degradation or weak sequencing
falsification_conditions: sequence and maintenance are already bounded
cooling cost is structurally explained elsewhere
allowed_claim_language: Chiller degradation is a plausible cooling-loss hypothesis requiring sequence and maintenance validation.
prohibited_claim_language: This site has an inefficient chiller.
financial_exposure_if_true: cooling CAPEX may target the wrong variable or wrong sequence
maintenance and controls action may outrank equipment replacement
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to schedule, envelope or process rivals
stop_conditions: performance and maintenance evidence are bounded enough to rank the hypothesis
escalation_conditions: field or BAS review required only if documentary evidence remains insufficient
example_outputs: Before funding chiller replacement, determine whether sequence, fouling or weak maintenance is the real cooling problem.
tests: building and cooling-intensive cases should admit this when chiller evidence is unresolved
pattern must stay bounded at L2
